composition.actual_old_english: Se fiscere and his gefēra standað on ðǣm strande. Se gefēra cwið: “Saga mē, hwæt ðū hæbbe.” Se fiscere sægð, ðæt hē męte hæbbe. Hē hǣtt his gefēran ðone fisc beran. Se gefēra birð ðone fisc. Se fiscere cwið: “Ic gesēo ðē ðone fisc beran. Nū wāt ic, ðæt ðū mē hilpst.”
composition.independent_translation: The fisherman and his companion stand on the shore. The companion says, “Tell me what you have.” The fisherman says that he has food. He orders his companion to carry the fish. The companion carries the fish. The fisherman says, “I see you carrying the fish. Now I know that you help me.”
composition.judgment: Coherent connected exchange. First hē/his continues fisherman; following explicit companion subject resolves reference. Perception infinitive describes carrying, not a finite report. Hilpst governs dative mē; carried object is accusative.
